description: The wrong people in the right place trying to make a difference
summary: Our project is a video game intended for children ages 7-12, where they are tasked with micro- and macro-management of certain resources needed for the sustainability of astronauts in space. Considering games these days are mainly focused on engagement rather than learning, our project intends to teach younger audiences the consequences of failing a mission all the way beyond earth and how crucial research is. The importance this game provides is crucial for children to not only develop their cognitive skills but also their active system thinking.
details: 2036 is an interactivity-based survival and resource management game aimed to teach children aged between 7-12 about the real world engineering compromises that happen during deep space exploration. The game puts you in the role of an pioneering astronaut in the year 2036 who must manage 3 different resources to survive on the moon. These resources are Oxygen, Radiation Protection and Food. Your goal is to manage these resources until they reach safe levels to sustain Artemis crews. The game uses real space weather events provided by NASA’s DONKI (Space Weather Database). This means there is no free choices. During solar storms you must sacrifice your oxygen or hydroponics to protect your radiation protection. The game is very easy to understand with simple tooltips, lots of replayability and clear explanations of where the information comes from within the game. It was also made using Godot Engine which uses python language in coding. In our project demonstration, we utilized HTML to show the game's desired product.
